Subject Youth's National Salvation Service Group - activities
on October 19.

Made by Kao Yen-ken Forwarded by C Gueye (签名)

Under the auspices of the Youth's National Salvation
Service Group, 370 Avenue Edward VII, about 100 representatives
of local national salvation bodies held a meeting in the Sing
Jao (新桥) Primary School, Sing Jao Ka, Nantao, off Rue
Brenier de Montmorand, between 10 a.m. and 12 noon October 19,
to commemorate the 1st anniversary of the death of Loo Sing,
a noted novelist and writer on proletarian subjects. Mr. Chang
Yu-liang (張裕良), Chairman of the Youth's National Salvation
Service Group, presided and delivered a speech eulogizing the
works of the deceased and urging the support of the campaign
of resistance against Japanese aggression for the sake of the
Chinese race. Similar speeches were made by several others.
The meeting was concluded with the shouting of slogans appropriate
to the occasion.
(specimen)
During the proceedings, copies of a handbill (attached)
containing a manifesto bearing on the anniversary issued by the
Youth's National Salvation Service Group were distributed among
those present. The manifesto contained the following
slogans :-
1. In commemoration of the death of Mr. Loo Sing, we must
exterminate Chinese traitors !
2. In commemoration of the death of Mr. Loo Sing, we must
strengthen the power of the masses to resist the
Japanese aggression !

In the afternoon of October 19, groups, each con-
sisting of five or six persons, carried out similar propaganda
in Shanghai. Only four parties functioned in the Settlement,
distributing a number of copies of the above-mentioned handbill.

日期：1937年10月20日

主题：青年救国服务团——10月19日的活动

制作人：高延肯（Kao Yen-ken） 转呈人：C Gueye (签名)

在青年救国服务团（地址：爱多亚路370号）的主持下，约100名本地救国团体的代表于10月19日上午10时至中午12时，在南市勃兰纳蒙莫朗路（Rue Brenier de Montmorand）旁的新桥卡（Sing Jao Ka）新桥小学举行会议，纪念著名无产阶级题材小说家及作家鲁迅（Loo Sing）逝世一周年。青年救国服务团主席张裕良先生主持会议并发表演讲，颂扬逝者的著作，并呼吁为了中华民族支持抗日运动。另有数人发表了类似演讲。会议在呼喊适合当时场合的口号中结束。
（样本）
在会议进行期间，向与会者分发了由青年救国服务团发布的、载有纪念周年宣言的传单副本（附后）。该宣言包含以下口号：
1. 为纪念鲁迅先生逝世，我们必须铲除汉奸！
2. 为纪念鲁迅先生逝世，我们必须加强民众抵抗日本侵略的力量！

10月19日下午，各小组（每组由五至六人组成）在上海进行了类似的宣传活动。仅在公共租界内有四个小组开展活动，分发了若干份上述传单。

and "Contribution Soliciting Party" respectively (specimens

October 16, 1937.
Afternoon Translation.

Lih Pao and other local newspapers:

LATE MR. LU SIN TO BE COMMEMORATED

At a joint meeting held by various youths' national salvation associations yesterday, the following resolutions were passed:-
1) That a mammoth service in memory of the late Mr. Lu Sin ( 魯迅 ), a noted Chinese writer, be held.
2) That contributions of cotton vests in memory of the late writer be solicited from the public.
3) That a "Committee to Commemorate the late Mr. Lu Sin" be formed, with offices at the premises of the Youths' National Salvation Service Group, to take up the necessary preparations for the above matters.

In memory of the late writer, the Shanghai War-time Literature and Art Association will hold a meeting at the Women's Y.M.C.A., Moulmein Road, at 1 p.m. October 18, when Mrs. Lu Sin, nee Hsu Kwang-ping ( 許廣平 ), will give a lecture on the life of her husband and an exhibition of manuscripts of writings of Mr. Lu Sin will be held.

October 19 being the anniversary of the death of Mr. Lu Sin, various local bodies are making preparations for commemoration.

Lih Pao:

OPEN LETTER TO FORMOSANS IN SOUTH CHINA

In support of the war of resistance now being fought by China against Japan, the Chinese Formosan Revolutionary League yesterday issued the following open letter to Formosans living in various parts of South China:-
"Dear Brethren,
"If we want to live and be free, let us unite and launch a ruthless attack on the Japanese Imperialists! The 450,000,000 people of China, our fatherland, have already formed themselves into a mass as strong as steel and are displaying united resistance against Japan. It is time for the 4,500,000 Formosan brethren to avenge themselves and settle their bloody account. Let us all do our share in supplementing and strengthening the sacred resistance of our fatherland, until we succeed in gaining the final victory!"

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram):

REFUGEES IN INTERIOR NOT TO PROCEED TO SHANGHAI

The Executive Yuan on October 15 issued an order to the various provincial and city governments to the effect that in order to avoid any untoward consequences that might arise from the relief problem, all refugees in the interior should be advised to refrain from proceeding to Shanghai until such time the war in that area is settled.

on November 18th 1937 at above address Tseu Tseng was not at home
and from his wife it was learned that since leaving his position
as Chinese Police Watchman he had become a money lender, therefore
he was engaged most of the time interviewing those who had obtain-
ed loans from him, consequently it was difficult to get in
contact with him. However, his wife was informed to tell him to
come and see the undersigned as soon as possible.
About 4 p.m. on November 18th 1937 Tseu Tseng called at the
Senior Detective's office and he was told that he had been marked
as a traitor by the Shanghai Municipality Students War Time
Service Group, therefore he was strongly advised to remove to
another address owing to the danger that exists when such a record
is kept at a patriotic organisation as mentioned. However, he
stated about a month ago two Chinese dressed in foreign clothes
had told his house master named Ling Cheng Woo(林成武) that he was
a traitor, but he did not see the men and, he had nothing to
fear as he had no connection whatever with the Japanese. Tseu
Tseng said he would remain at his present address, because Ling
Cheng Woo owed him $180.00 and he is almost sure the allegation
about him being employed by the Japanese to do traitor's work
possibly originated from one of the persons who owes him money.
It would appear this is a clear exposition of how such
patriotic organisations can be utilised to satisfy the ends of a
disgruntled person (s) and there is every reason for those who
obtain a loan from him to be so, because he is charging as much
as 50 to 60 per cent on money advanced.

1937年11月18日，在上述地址，周正不在家，从其妻子处得知，自从辞去华捕巡捕职务后，他成为了一名放贷人，因此他大部分时间都在面见那些从他那里获得贷款的人，因而很难与他取得联系。不过，已告知其妻子让他尽快来见本人。
1937年11月18日下午4时许，周正来到高级侦探办公室，被告知他被上海市学生战时服务团标记为汉奸，因此强烈建议他搬离现址，因为正如前述，当此类记录保存在爱国组织时存在危险。然而，他表示大约一个月前，两名穿着西装的中国人告诉他的房东林成武（Ling Cheng Woo），他是汉奸，但他并未见到这些人，而且他无所畏惧，因为他与日本人没有任何联系。周正表示他将留在现址，因为林成武欠他180.00美元，他几乎可以肯定，关于他受雇于日本人从事汉奸活动的指控可能源自某个欠他钱的人。
这似乎清楚地说明了这类爱国组织如何被利用来满足不满者的目的，而那些从他那里获得贷款的人有理由这样做，因为他对预付款项收取高达50%至60%的利息。

November 4, 1937.

Dear Sirs,

We have just received a letter from the Shanghai
Municipality Citizens Committee for the Severance of
Economic Relations with Japan to the following effect:-

"We have received from your Chamber letters
Nos.4694, 4710, 4734, 4795, 4764, 4785, 4793, 4803,
and 4805 together with proposals submitted by various
trade associations relating to the time limit for the
registration of Japanese goods, the percentage of the
value for the purchase of Liberty Bonds, and safekeeping
and auction of the goods, etc. These proposals have
been discussed at joint meetings of the executive and
supervisory committees of this Committee, and the
following resolutions have been reached:-

1. That the registration of Japanese goods be extended
7 days until November 7. The various trade associa-
tions have to register the Japanese goods in their
stock as soon as possible as no further extension
will be granted.

2.That 80% of the proceeds obtained from the auction
of the goods be used for the purchase of Liberty
Bonds, instead of 50% as previously agreed upon.

3. As regards the proposals relating to the concentra-
tion of Japanese goods for safe-keeping and auction,
measures regarding this matter have been promulgated.
However, this committee will engage experts to make
a further study of the proposals.

China Evening News of Oct.17:

COMMITTEE FOR SEVERANCE OF ECONOMIC RELATIONS TO
REGISTER ENEMY GOODS

The following is a report on the progress being
made in the works of the recently inaugurated Shanghai
People's Committee for the Severance of Economic Relations
with Japan:-
(1) Severance of commercial relations. The
Committee will issue a public notification next week advising
merchants in various trades to register at specified places
the names and quantities of enemy goods which they had taken
into stock before August 13, the date on which local
hostilities broke out. The period for registration is
tentatively set at two weeks, at the expiration of which
measures for disposing of the said enemy goods will be
considered. At the same time, inspection parties will be
organized by the Examination Section of the Committee for the
purpose of ascertaining enemy goods, either disguised or
undisguised, taken into stock by traitorous merchants after
August 13.
(2) Severance of employment relations. The
Committee will register Chinese employees of local Japanese
firms, banks, companies and shops and will decide upon the
measures for giving them employment after their number has
been ascertained.
(3) Severance of financial relations. The
Committee has already written to the Bankers' Association and
the Native Bankers' Association asking them to study and carry
out the proposal.

Drastic measures for the rigid

boycott were adopted during the

Committee of the Shanghai As-
sociation for Severance of Economic
Relations with Japanese yester-
day according to an official an-
nouncement today.

Highlights of the decisions
reached yesterday for enforcement
with official support include:

1 Business establishments hold-
ing stocks of Japanese goods

sociation before the end of Octo-
ber in order that the cargoes may
be concentrated and sold under

To Confiscate Goods

goods after the registration shall
be punished with confiscation of
the goods and the responsible
persons shall be punished ac-
cording to law.

4 The Chamber of Commerce
shall be asked to order all mer-
chants to nullify all contracts en-
tered into with Japanese and re-
port such to the association.

5 Transactions in raw materials
shall be treated as transactions
in manufactured goods.

General Boycott

6 All public organs shall be
notified to inform their members
and subordinates not to work in
Japanese business establishments
and households, not to use Japan-
ese warehouses not to travel on

Japanese money and not to have
any connection with Japanese
banks.

stitutions shall be told to sever all

Japanese.

MEASURES DECIDED UPON FOR SEVERANCE OF ECONOMIC RELATIONS
WITH JAPAN

At a meeting held at 10 a.m. yesterday by the
Shanghai People's Committee for the Severance of Economic
Relations with Japan, at which Mr. Wong Shiao-lai and some
20 others were present, the following resolutions were
discussed and passed:-
1) That the regulations governing the formation of the
Executive Committee be revised and approved.
2) That the National Government be requested to prevent
people from entering into commercial relations with the
enemy and to decide upon measures for the punishment of
those who are found to have helped the enemy by means of
economic services.
3) That the following measures be decided upon to deal with
the present stock in Shanghai of Japanese goods:-
a) That the owners of those Japanese goods which were
purchased before August 13 apply for registration with
this Committee not later than the end of October.
After this the registered goods will be kept for safe
custody in the hands of the various trade associations
concerned under the instructions of this Committee
and will be sold at auction; 50% of the proceeds thus
derived will be contributed towards the fund for the
purchase of Liberty Bonds.
b) That all Japanese goods purchased after August 13 be
confiscated as soon as they are discovered.
c) That owners or other responsible persons be severely
dealt with according to law, in addition to the
confiscation of their goods, if they are found to have
failed to apply for registration with this Committee
of the goods which they possess, or if they are found
to have secretly disposed of their goods even though
a registration has been made with this Committee.
4) That the Chamber of Commerce be notified to instruct all
the trade associations to cancel all agreements previously
concluded with Japanese merchants for the purchase of
Japanese goods and report to this Committee the result
of their efforts for reference sake.
5) That transactions in raw materials be dealt with in a
similar way to other Japanese goods.
6) That all the local public bodies be notified to instruct
their subordinate organs and individuals to refuse
employment with any factories or commercial organs or
families of the enemy, to abstain from using enemy ware-
houses, to refrain from boarding enemy merchantmen, and
to refuse accepting or circulating enemy goods or money
or entering into relations with the enemy banks.
7) That the Standing Committee be asked to draw up a set of
regulations governing the People's Severance of Economic
Relations with Japan and a movement be started to urge
the people to swear in this connection.

2) 请国民政府防止人民与敌人建立商业关系，并决定对被发现通过经济服务帮助敌人者实施惩处的措施。
3) 决定采取以下措施处理上海现有的日货库存：-
a) 8月13日之前购买的日货所有者，须不迟于十月底向本委员会申请登记。此后，登记的货物将在本委员会的指导下，由各相关同业公会妥善保管并进行拍卖；由此所得款项的50%将捐入购买救国公债基金。
b) 8月13日之后购买的所有日货，一经发现即予没收。
c) 如果发现拥有货物者未向本委员会申请登记，或者虽然已向本委员会登记但秘密处置货物，除没收其货物外，还将依法严惩业主或其他责任人。
4) 通知总商会指示所有同业公会取消此前与日商签订的购买日货的所有协议，并将努力结果报告本委员会以备查考。
5) 原材料交易的处理方式与其他日货类似。
6) 通知所有地方公共团体指示其下属机构和个人，拒绝受雇于敌人的任何工厂、商业机构或家庭，避免使用敌人仓库， refrain from boarding enemy merchantmen（原文不清，意为：避免登上敌国商船），并拒绝接受或流通敌国货物或货币，或与敌国银行建立关系。
7) 请常务委员会起草一套关于民众断绝与日本经济关系的规章，并发起运动敦促民众就此宣誓。

Nanking Road Store Buys Enemy Goods: Investigation
Being Made

Upon receipt of information to the effect that
a certain large store on Nanking Road had recently effected
the removal of more than 100 cases of enemy goods from the
warehouses of Butterfield & Swire, the various local public
bodies detailed officials to conduct enquiries into the
true facts of the case. As a result, it has been
ascertained that these enemy goods have already been disguised

disposal. Efforts are being made by the various local
bodies to ascertain the names of the principal figures in
connection with this affair and the places to which these
goods have been transported as well as the names of the
shipping hongs with a view to bringing about effective
sanctions.

Manifesto

The following is the gist of the manifesto, issued
in the name of the inauguration meeting of the Shanghai
People's Committee for the Severance of Economic Relations
with Japan:-
"(1) It is our opinion that, in addition to
armed force,severance of economic relations can also be
used as a weapon to resist our enemy. Japan's capitalism
is built on an extremely weak foundation. Her idea of
promoting a Sino-Japanese rapprochement is to seize control
of China's vast natural resources and market. Upon
failing to succeed in this, she resorts to forceful plunder.
In doing this, the Japanese Imperialists are digging their
own grave.
"(2) Since the beginning of our war of resistance,
Japan has increased her budgetary estimates from
Y.3,000,000,000 to Y.5,000,000,000. At the present rate
of consumption, this sum is only sufficient to support the
Japanese fighting forces for ten months. We know that
most of the cotton mills and cotton exchanges in Japan have
already suspended business; the economic terror created
by her is spreading like an epidemic. This, together with
a serious blow from the outside, will bring about a break-
down of the Japanese armed forces.
"(3) The inhuman acts committed by the Japanese
Imperialists in China have aroused the indignation of all
peace-loving and just peoples of the world. An aggressive
force can never compete with the world's peaceful force.
"(4) The peoples of friendly Powers have already
started to deal an economic blow to Japan. It is up to
us to increase our endeavour and strictly carry out a
severance of economic relations with Japan, so as to
accelerate the ruin of the Japanese Imperialists.
"(5) The weapon of severance of economic relations
is now in our hands. If we will hurl it continuously at
the enemy, it will surely break down the economic support
behind them and cause their defeat on the field and
revolutionary uprising in their country. Let every
Chinese people carry out this movement with the spirit of
the men at the front."

Circular Telegram

The circular telegram, which is addressed to all
public organs and bodies, newspapers, schools and people
throughout the country, urges various circles in different
parts of the country to form organizations for the purpose
of bringing about severance of economic relations with Japan.

The Shanghai Various Circles' Enemy-Resisting
Support Association on October 9 decided to dispatch a
telegram to the National Government requesting it to recall
the Chinese Ambassador to Japan and to prohibit Chinese
people from trading with the enemy.

选举潘公展等14人为监察委员会委员，并提出并通过了一份宣言和一份通电。

宣言

以下是以上海民众对日绝交经济关系委员会成立大会名义发布的宣言要点：
“(1) 我方认为，除武力外，断绝经济关系亦可作为抵抗敌人的一种武器。日本的资本主义建立在极其薄弱的基础之上。其提倡中日亲善的理念，意在夺取控制中国丰富的自然资源和广阔市场。在此企图失败后，便诉诸强力掠夺。日本帝国主义者此举实乃自掘坟墓。
“(2) 自抗战开始以来，日本已将其预算估计从30亿日元增加至50亿日元。按目前的消耗速度，这笔款项仅够维持日本军队十个月之久。据悉，日本大多数棉纺厂和棉花交易所已停止营业；由其造成的经济恐慌正像瘟疫般蔓延。这种情况，加上来自外部的沉重打击，将导致日本武装力量的崩溃。
“(3) 日本帝国主义者在中国犯下的非人道行径，激起了全世界所有爱好和平与正义人民的愤慨。侵略势力永远无法与世界和平力量相抗衡。
“(4) 友好国家的人民已经开始对日本实施经济打击。我们应加倍努力，严格执行对日经济绝交，以加速日本帝国主义的灭亡。
“(5) 经济绝交的武器现已掌握在我们手中。如果我们持续将其投向敌人，必将摧毁其背后的经济支撑，导致其在战场上失败并在其国内引发革命起义。愿全体中国人民以前线将士的精神开展此项运动。”

通电

这份致全国各公共机关和团体、报纸、学校及人民的通电，敦促全国各地各界组建组织，以实现与日本断绝经济关系之目的。
